1	# Agent Note: Shifts, the always-on driver of the Daliesk Village
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-village-shifts.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	The [Daliesk Village note](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md) describes an always-running lab, and its shift zero runs with a human on call because nothing in the repository runs a plan more than once or survives a restart. `ctx.fleet.run(plan)` executes one plan inside one process and returns one report; when the process dies mid-plan, the cells already run survive only as session logs nobody indexes, the cells never started are forgotten, and a restarted process that runs the same plan again mints a new group and produces a second session for cells that already have one. The [four-goal note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) names the missing piece in its rollout item 11 as durable orchestration, with cells idempotent by header hash × environment × repetition that recover from persisted child sessions, and the Village note's rollout item 3 makes unattended shifts depend on it. Four gaps stand between the fleet and an unattended shift: no durable identity for a shift, so a restart cannot tell a resumed plan from a new one; no per-cell durable record, so recovery has to be rebuilt from every session log; no cadence, so nothing starts the next shift and nothing keeps two shifts of one district from overlapping; and no spend window across shifts, so the fleet's per-plan ceiling is the only thing between a provider incident and a month of inference budget spent in one night.
10	
11	## Proposal
12	
13	Three details settled during slices 1 and 2. `ctx.fleet.run` gained an optional `cells` selection out of the plan's own enumeration, because a `FleetPlan` is a cross product and a resumed shift's pending set is not one — without it a resumed cell would run at repetition zero and double-count in its group. A district's plan names its model routes rather than falling back to the composition's default route, because the driver enumerates its own cells to compute a pending set and to digest the plan, and a digest that moved with another plugin's current selection would not freeze anything. The driver reads the environment registry through `ctx.get('environments')` rather than declaring it, keeping the Loader requirement at `fleet`, `sessions`, and `sessionPersistence`; a slot that cannot reach the registry is refused with `SHIFT_INVALID_PLAN`.
14	
15	A `@deepseek-ai/dsh-shifts` plugin under `packages/improvement/shifts` providing `ctx.shifts`: a durable loop over the fleet that freezes each shift's identity, records the shift in its own session log, resumes an interrupted shift by running only the cells that never started, and refuses a shift that would overrun its district's spend window. The session event log stays the sole authority: the shift ledger is a set of `shift/*` events in a shift session, cells are recovered from the `environment/run` stamps their sessions already carry, and the driver holds nothing in memory that a restart needs.
16	
17	### Shift identity
18	
19	`shiftDigest(plan)` is the SHA-256 hex over `{ version, district, environments, models, repetitions, tokenCeiling }`, with the environment ids sorted by code unit after a filter is resolved against the registry at freeze time and the routes kept in listing order, following `planDigest` in `dsh-experiments`; `workspaceRoot`, the cadence, and the spend window are deployment choices and stay out of it. A shift instance is `shift-<digest>-<scheduledAt>`, the slot time in epoch milliseconds, so two processes computing the same slot compute the same identity without counting anything. The shift id is the `group` on every cell's stamp, so the sessions of one shift are grouped durably the way `experiment-<digest>-<arm>` groups an arm, and the scorekeeper's per-group pass@k needs no new field.
20	
21	### The shift ledger
22	
23	The driver creates one session per slot, as the runner creates one per cell, and appends to it: `shift/start { shiftId, digest, plan, scheduledAt }` with the frozen plan verbatim; `shift/cell { shiftId, cell, sessionId, outcome }` per cell once its outcome is in hand, `outcome` being `reported` with its `certified` flag, `error` with the fleet's code, or `interrupted` for an orphan found on resume; `shift/resume { shiftId, done, pending }` when a later process picks the shift up; `shift/skipped { digest, scheduledAt, reason }` with `reason` in `spend-window | overlap` when the slot is refused, in which case the slot's session holds that one event and no `shift/start`; and `shift/end { shiftId, outcome, spend, cells }` with `outcome` in `completed | ceiling | stopped`, where `spend` is the fleet report's token sum and `cells` the counts per outcome. Every event is appended after the fact it records is durable, never before. Cost in EUR is not a shift field: the scorekeeper folds it from `usage/priced` events under the Village note's rule that cost is a logged fact or is not published.
24	
25	### Idempotent cells and resume
26	
27	A cell is identified by its shift id, environment, model route, and repetition, all present on the `environment/run` stamp. On start, the driver lists persisted sessions through `ctx.sessionPersistence.list()`, loads every shift session whose log has a `shift/start` without a `shift/end`, and for each such shift computes the pending cells as the plan's cells minus those with a `shift/cell` entry minus those whose stamp exists in a session created at or after the shift session (header `createdAt`, which bounds the scan to sessions younger than the shift). A cell whose session exists but never ended is an orphan: it is recorded as `shift/cell` with `outcome: interrupted` and is never run again under the same repetition, because a second session for the same cell would double-count in pass@k and hide the crash; the crash is an outcome of the harness under test and stays an error row. The resumed shift runs the pending cells through `ctx.fleet.run` with the same group and district and with the plan's token ceiling reduced by the usage folded from every session the shift already has, then appends `shift/end`. The fleet gains one observe-only Cordis event, `fleet/cell { group, district, cell, outcome }`, emitted after each cell's outcome is recorded, so the ledger is written per cell rather than once per plan; the scan by stamp remains the authority whenever the ledger is behind.
28	
29	### Cadence and spend window
30	
31	Config: `workspaceRoot`; `districts`, a list of `{ district, plan, cadence: { intervalMs }, spendWindow?: { windowMs, maxTokens } }`; `startImmediately`. One shift per district is in flight at a time; the next slot of a district is the previous `shift/start.scheduledAt` plus `intervalMs`, read from the ledger, so a restart neither drifts nor doubles a slot; slots that passed while no process ran leave no record and are not caught up, the hole being visible from the slot arithmetic; a slot that arrives while the district's previous shift still runs is refused with `shift/skipped { reason: overlap }`. Before a shift starts, the driver folds `shift/end.spend` over the district's slots inside `windowMs`; a start that would begin with the window exhausted appends `shift/skipped { reason: spend-window }` and creates no cell session. The per-cell caps stay with the budget policy and the per-plan ceiling with the fleet; the window is the third layer, across plans, that the Village note's budgets section asks for.
32	
33	### Process and supervision
34	
35	The driver starts its loop on the application's ready event and stops on disposal: the in-flight fleet run is cancelled through its signal, in-flight cells end as the runner ends them, and their sessions become the orphans the next process records. A host-level supervisor, a systemd unit with `Restart=always` or a container restart policy, restarts the process; the README ships the unit file and the on-call runbook for the five conditions of the Village note (a crashed orchestrator, a route-wide outage past the retry budget, a full disk, a dead shift timer, a hung tool call), stating which the ledger makes visible (the first two and the timer, through a `shift/start` with no `shift/end` and a district with no recent slot) and which it does not (the disk and a hung call). Composition through the Loader requires `fleet`, `sessions`, and `sessionPersistence`; `verify-village-composition` already covers a shift composition because it composes the fleet.
36	
37	## Alternatives considered
38	
39	**A cron job around a fleet script.** Rejected: stateless; a restart or a second invocation runs the whole plan again under a new group, and nothing records that a slot was skipped or why.
40	
41	**A workflow-engine program on the worker-thread engine.** Rejected for now: the current engine journals nothing, so a program dies with its process; the four-goal note's item 11 pairs the journaling engine with the program ledger, and this driver is the smallest durable loop such an engine can later host without changing the ledger events.
42	
43	**Re-running an interrupted cell at the same repetition.** Rejected: the orphan session already carries the stamp, so the scorekeeper would see two sessions for one cell in one group; the crash is a harness outcome and belongs in the error column, and a shift with many interrupted cells is itself a finding.
44	
45	**A ledger file beside the session logs.** Rejected: a second authority that persistence, replay, the session query tool, and the invariant companions know nothing about; the shift session reuses all of them.
46	
47	**Ledger entries inside the cell sessions.** Rejected: a slot refused for its spend window would have no record at all, and a cell session belongs to the runner.
48	
49	## Acceptance criteria
50	
51	- A Loader-booted e2e runs a two-district composition through the driver, terminates the process after the first cell's session is durable, restarts it on the same persistence root, and the resumed shift keeps its group, appends `shift/resume` with the right pending set, runs only the cells with no session, records the orphan as `interrupted`, and the scoreboard shows one row per cell with the orphan as an error and never a duplicate environment, route, and repetition.
52	- `shiftDigest` is stable under environment reordering and changes with the repetitions, the routes, the district, or the token ceiling; a `shift/start` whose `plan` re-digests to another value fails the invariant companion.
53	- The invariant companion rejects a `shift/cell` before its `shift/start`, two `shift/cell` entries for one cell in one shift, and a `shift/end` before `shift/start`, each with a failing fixture.
54	- A spend window of one token yields `shift/skipped { reason: spend-window }` and no cell session; a slot arriving during a running shift yields `shift/skipped { reason: overlap }`.
55	- The fleet's `fleet/cell` event fires once per cell after the outcome is recorded, asserted in the fleet's existing e2e.
56	- The README pair carries the unit file, the runbook, and a Model Experience section stating that nothing here enters a model request; the Village note's rollout item 3 points here.
57	
58	## Rollout
59	
60	1. Landed. Fleet: the observe-only `fleet/cell` event with its unit and e2e assertions, plus the `cells` selection slice 2 needs to run a subset of one plan through `ctx.fleet.run`.
61	2. Landed. `dsh-shifts`: the digest, the shift session and `shift/*` events, resume by ledger and stamp scan, cadence, spend window, the invariant companion, a Loader-booted e2e with kill and restart, the README pair, the persistence catalog regenerated. The README also carries slice 4's unit file, container example, and runbook, so an operator reading the package has them before the gate message exists.
62	3. Scorekeeper: `shiftFacts`, one row per shift from the ledger, and the `district` column of `ScoreboardRow`, closing the Village note's TODO.
63	4. Supervision: the `verify-village-composition` message naming the driver when a shift composition lacks persistence; the unit file, the container example, and the runbook landed with slice 2.
64	5. Later, the journaling workflow engine of the four-goal note hosts the loop; the ledger events do not change.
65	
66	## Risks
67	
68	- **Scan cost on resume.** A persistence root with thousands of sessions makes the stamp scan slow; bounding it to sessions created after the shift session keeps it proportional to one shift, and the `fleet/cell` entries make the scan the exception.
69	- **Clock.** The cadence reads the host clock; a clock jump moves a slot and never doubles one, because the ledger decides.
70	- **Orphans in an incident.** A provider outage that kills cells mid-run inflates the error column; the fleet's route breaker limits it per plan, the spend window per district, and the rows stay truthful by design.
71	- **Disk.** Workspace retention exists; log retention does not, so a deployment that runs for months needs a retention plan for session logs before shift zero starts.
72	- **Two descriptions during rollout item 1.** Until the scorekeeper folds the ledger, the fleet report and the ledger both describe a shift; the ledger is the one a restart reads.
73

1	# Agent Note: Shared session-event validator plumbing
2	
3	Status: implemented
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-06-shared-session-event-validator-plumbing.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Several package-owned invariant companions check a durable session-event relation against the events committed immediately before each candidate. Each implements the same two-phase shape by hand: replay every already-loaded session's committed events in order, then subscribe to Cordis's `internal/dispatch` and re-check every future `session/event` dispatch against the dispatching session's currently committed events — the events immediately preceding the candidate, since Session dispatches before publishing it. `dsh-budget-policy`, `dsh-goal-round-driver`, and `dsh-scorekeeper` implemented this identically enough that `pnpm run duplication` flagged their seed loops as clones of each other. `dsh-shifts`, `dsh-experiments`, and `dsh-tool-todo` carried the same plumbing under a `jscpd:ignore` marker that existed only to hide the same duplication from the gate.
10	
11	## Decision
12	
13	`@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants` exports `sessionEventValidator(validate, sessions)`, an `InvariantInstaller` factory:
14	
15	```ts
16	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
17	import type { InvariantFailure, InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
18	
19	declare function sessionEventValidator<TEvent>(
20	  validate: (prior: readonly TEvent[], event: TEvent, fail: InvariantFailure) => void,
21	  sessions: (ctx: Context) => Iterable<{ readonly events: readonly TEvent[] }>,
22	): InvariantInstaller
23	```
24	
25	`validate` is the package-owned relation check; `sessions` is the calling package's own session accessor, always `ctx => ctx.sessions.list()` in every current caller. The returned installer runs `validate` for every event already committed to each session `sessions` returns, threading the events preceding each one as `prior`, then subscribes to `internal/dispatch` and runs `validate` again for every live `session/event` dispatch, passing the dispatching session's committed events as `prior`. It injects the `sessions` service — the same dependency every hand-rolled version already declared.
26	
27	The helper is generic over the caller's session and event types rather than importing `Session`/`SessionEvent` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`: that package's own `./invariant` companion already depends on `dsh-invariants`, so an import running the other way would form a circular package reference. `dsh-budget-policy`, `dsh-goal-round-driver`, `dsh-scorekeeper`, `dsh-shifts`, `dsh-experiments`, and `dsh-tool-todo` build their installer this way, deleting their private seed-loop and dispatch-listener copies and every `jscpd:ignore` marker that existed only to hide this duplication.
28	
29	`scripts/package-invariants.ts`'s static check — which requires a non-empty installer to accept and visibly use its bound failure reporter — recognizes a `sessionEventValidator(validate, sessions)` call the same way it already recognized a direct `(ctx, fail) => …` installer and an `Object.assign(fn, { inject })` wrapper: it resolves `validate` (an inline function or a local named-function reference in the same file) and checks that function's own last parameter, since `sessionEventValidator` never hides or drops it.
30	
31	Companions whose per-event check needs more than the committed session-event log keep their own installers: `dsh-permission-presets` also needs an injected service beyond `sessions` to resolve a preset reference, and `dsh-commands` keys mutable per-session state by `Session` object identity rather than recomputing from a `prior` events array (`dsh-read-barrier` needs the `Session` object the same way). `dsh-schedule` refolds the whole session stream per candidate rather than checking one event against its prefix. `dsh-llm-retry` and `dsh-time-context` add a `session/created` listener and branch across more than one per-event-type check function. A larger family — `dsh-goal`, `dsh-verification`, `dsh-hook-protocol`, `dsh-user-approval`, `dsh-compaction`, `dsh-session`, `dsh-tools`, and `dsh-tool-workflow` — carries per-session incremental fold state across three listeners (seed, `session/created`, and a staged `internal/dispatch`/`session/event` commit pair), a different plumbing shape this helper does not cover. `dsh-sandbox-policy` is a verbatim instance of the shape this helper extracts and remains a candidate for the same migration.
32	
33	## Alternatives considered
34	
35	- **A base class or mixin the companions extend.** Rejected: `InvariantInstaller` is a plain function value, and Cordis plugin composition already expects `apply`/`inject` exports rather than inheritance; a factory function matches the existing shape without a new composition mechanism.
36	- **Import `Session`/`SessionEvent` from `dsh-session` for a precisely-typed helper.** Rejected: `dsh-session`'s own invariant companion depends on `dsh-invariants`, so the reverse import would form a circular TypeScript project reference and a circular package dependency. Genericity over the caller-supplied session/event shape avoids both at the cost of one accessor parameter per caller.
37	- **Force every companion sharing the seed-and-dispatch outer loop onto this signature regardless of what its check needs.** Rejected for `dsh-permission-presets` and `dsh-commands`: their checks need an extra injected service or session-identity-keyed mutable state the `(prior, event, fail)` signature does not carry, and reshaping them to fit would change their own logic, not just extract shared wiring.
38	- **Extend the helper to also cover the stage-then-commit companions.** Rejected: that shape carries per-session incremental fold state across two additional listeners the seed-and-dispatch shape does not need; unifying them would either force the simpler companions to carry unused state or complicate the helper for callers that do not need it.
39	
40	## Consequences
41	
42	- `pnpm run duplication` no longer flags the three originally-cloned seed loops, and six companions no longer carry a `jscpd:ignore` marker whose only purpose was hiding this duplication.
43	- A new companion with this exact shape adds one `validate` function and one `sessionEventValidator(validate, ctx => ctx.sessions.list())` call instead of re-deriving the seed-and-dispatch wiring; `scripts/package-invariants.ts` accepts the pattern without a companion-specific carve-out.
44	- `dsh-invariants` still imports no product package: the helper's `sessions` and event types are caller-supplied generics, and the service still owns none of the six companions' actual relation checks.
45	- `dsh-permission-presets`, `dsh-commands`, `dsh-read-barrier`, `dsh-schedule`, `dsh-llm-retry`, `dsh-time-context`, `dsh-sandbox-policy`, and the stage-then-commit family keep their own hand-rolled installers; their outer-loop resemblance to the extracted shape remains, but jscpd's clone threshold does not flag it, and — outside `dsh-sandbox-policy` — forcing them onto the new signature would change what each depends on or computes.
46

1	# Agent Note: Content-addressed identity and the composition manifest event
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-composition-manifest.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Every identity in the harness names a slot rather than the bytes in it. A `ComponentId` is "derived from its kind and the owning seam's stable name, never from mount order" ([`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md)), a skill is addressed by its kebab-case name, a prompt section and a tool by their registered names, a preset by its directory name, and a plugin by its package name. Editing a skill body in place leaves all of those addresses unchanged, so a leaderboard cannot separate the generation before the edit from the generation after it, a rollback has no earlier address to return to, and a decontamination check has nothing to key on — the failure the [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) records under its rejected "single mutable knowledge store" alternative and forbids in principle P5.
10	
11	Nothing durable records which components a session had in play. The `request/header` event carries each epoch's assembled system prompt text and tool schemas, which is enough to replay a request and not enough to name what produced it: it carries no component identity, provenance, lineage, or registry layer; a skill body loaded through the `skill` tool reaches the transcript as a tool result and never the header; and a dynamic package mounted through [`tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) that registers no tool is invisible in it. The component registry itself is composition-time state that dies with the process, as [the component-registry seam note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) states outright.
12	
13	Four consumers are blocked on that gap. [`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) ships no `composition_hash`, `component_ids`, or `skills_used` field because no event supplies one. W4 stage 1's invariant — a skill result whose digest is absent from the manifest fails — has no manifest to check against. The trajectory exporter can withhold a held-out environment but cannot tell a curated composition from one an agent mutated mid-session, so a synthesized skill body can reach a training set unannounced. And W4 stage 9's knowledge ledger has no address to mirror its entries against, which is what makes "a ledger entry with no matching manifest occurrence never counts as having been in play" enforceable rather than aspirational.
14	
15	## Proposal
16	
17	**One digest function, one address form.** [`dsh-components`](../../../../packages/components/components/README.md) gains `ComponentDigest` (a `Branded<'ComponentDigest'>` from `dsh-brand`) and two pure functions: `componentDigest(kind, canonical)` returns the lowercase SHA-256 hex of `` `${kind}\n${JSON.stringify(canonical)}` ``, and `componentAddress(id, digest)` returns `` `${id}@${digest}` ``. The kind is inside the hashed bytes so two kinds whose canonical values coincide never share an address. The digest is the full 64 hex characters everywhere it is stored or compared, matching `environmentContentHashes` in [`dsh-environments`](../../../../packages/improvement/environments/README.md); truncating it for a card or a table is a presentation choice that never enters a log or the ledger. `ComponentDescriptor` gains a required `digest: ComponentDigest` and a required `digestBasis: 'content' | 'registration'`. As landed, `canonical` is typed `ComponentCanonical` — a JSON value — so a producer cannot hand the hash a value `JSON.stringify` would drop, and `componentAddress` returns a plain string: an address is minted and compared, never received across a boundary that a brand would guard.
18	
19	**Each producer owns its canonical value.** The registry ships no per-kind canonicalization for the same reason it ships no kind: each producer declares its `ComponentKindMap` member by declaration merging and exports the pure function that canonicalizes it, so a kind added later needs no change in the registry or in the manifest writer. The table below fixes the canonical value of every kind this note introduces. As landed, the exported function is the kind's digest rather than its bare canonical value — `agentProviderDigest(provider)`, and `skillDigest(definition)` as the skill row already names — so a consumer recomputing an address calls the producer instead of rebuilding the canonical value from the table.
20	
21	**The registry becomes layered.** `ComponentRegistry` was one flat `Map`, so it could not answer "what does this agent see". It uses `ScopedLayers` from `dsh-scope`, exactly as [`ctx.tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) and [`ctx.skills`](../../../../packages/skill/skill/README.md) already do: `register()` files into the calling context's scope, and `list({ kind, scope })` merges the global layer with the viewing scope's chain, the nearest layer's entry winning a duplicate id. A descriptor read back through a scope carries `layer: 'global' | 'agent'` — `global` when the winning registration sits in the global layer, `agent` when it sits in a layer of that agent's scope chain. A deeper chain still reads as `agent`, because a subagent writes its own manifest into its own session. Ids are unique per layer, so a duplicate in one layer still throws `COMPONENT_DUPLICATE_ID` while the same id in a different layer shadows.
22	
23	The derived `layer` rides `ComponentView`, a distinct read type extending `ComponentDescriptor`, rather than an optional descriptor field: a producer registers a descriptor and cannot assert its own layer, and a reader always has one. `get(id, { scope })` takes the same viewing scope as `list({ kind, scope })`, the `SkillViewOptions` pattern `dsh-skill` already uses for its two reads. The registry publishes no change notification — the rejected `components/change` alternative below is why — so the `ScopedLayers` change callback is an explained no-op.
24	
25	**The manifest writer reads one registry.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-components-manifest` at `packages/components/components-manifest/` injects `agents` and `components` and nothing else. On `agent/pre-step` it calls `next()` first, recomputes `ctx.components.list({ scope: agent })` for the calling agent, compares the resulting `compositionSha256` with the last `composition/manifest` event in that session's log, and appends a new event through `agent.session.append()` only when the two differ — the shape [`dsh-budget-policy`](../../../../packages/guard/budget-policy/README.md) already uses to fold and append before a step opens. Recomputing rather than tracking incrementally is what keeps it correct across HMR disposal, a preset mounted after creation, and scope shadowing: the writer holds no subscription state that any of those three orderings could invalidate.
26	
27	**Every other seam reaches the manifest through an adapter.** The one-adapter-per-seam rule [the component-registry note](2026-09-01-component-registry-seam.md) established is what keeps the writer from reading registries it does not own, and each adapter follows its seam's own change notification: `dsh-components-tools` follows `tools/change`, `dsh-components-prompt` follows `system-prompt/change`, `dsh-components-skills` follows `tools/result` for the `skill` tool, `dsh-components-presets` follows the `agent-preset/selected` Cordis event, and the shipped `dsh-components-subagents` already follows `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed`. One seam emits nothing today: the dynamic Cordis runner behind `tool-cordis` reports no change when a package is defined, run, stopped, or removed, so `dsh-cordis-host-runner` gains an unfiltered `cordis/dynamic-changed(agent, pluginId)` Cordis event — `@mode emit`, not scope-filtered, so no scope-scan metadata applies — and `dsh-components-packages` follows it.
28	
29	**A skill is in play once its body is loaded, not once it is listed.** `ctx.skills.list()` returns summaries without bodies, so registering every discoverable skill would need a body load per catalog entry per step and would still address a summary rather than the knowledge. `dsh-skill` therefore exports `skillDigest(definition)` over the loaded definition, the `skill` tool's canonical output value gains a `digest` field (absent from `renderSkillContent`, so the model-facing text is unchanged, and durable in `tool/result`), and `SkillInvocationSource` gains the same field so the user-explicit `/name` injection records it too. `dsh-components-skills` registers a `skill` component from either durable record through `exec.agent.ctx`, never by re-parsing the rendered `<skill_content>` block. Skills that were reachable but never loaded stay out of the manifest; the catalog they came from is already durable as the `skill-catalog` message source.
30	
31	**What slices 2 and 3 landed differently.** Five deviations, each the smallest the code admitted. The `tool` canonical value carries no output schema: `ToolSchema` — what `ctx.tools.schemas(scope)` projects and what the model receives — is name, description, and parameter schema, and the canonical output declaration is never model-visible, so addressing it would need the registry to project it beside the wire schema. The `prompt-section` adapter needs a registration read the prompt registry did not expose, so `SystemPrompt` gains `sections(scope?)`, the merged registrations in assembly order with each `text` as it stands. The `preset` adapter needs the trust, the composition path, and the resolved rows of a mount, none of which `PresetMount` carried, so `dsh-agent-presets` records `trust`, `path`, and `tree` on it; a row whose `config` does not survive the lossless-JSON boundary contributes `null`, exactly as an absent one does. That adapter also reconciles on `agent/created` beside `agent-preset/selected`, because a session that starts on the deployment default commits no selection event and the roster publishes no mount notification — `livePresetMounts()` reports a torn-down mount by pruning it, so reconciling against that reading is what removal is. And a `user`-trust preset is recorded with `provenance: 'synthesized'`: the roster records the root a preset was discovered under, never its author, and a locally authored composition carries the same trust as shell access.
32	
33	**What slices 4 and 5 landed differently.** Seven deviations. The `skill` tool's `digest` is not durable in `tool/result`: the tool registry keeps a canonical value out of durable events by design, so the digest reaches `dsh-components-skills` through the settled `tools/result` and the durable record of a loaded generation is the manifest entry that load causes, plus `SkillInvocationSource.digest` on the user-explicit path. `dsh-components-skills` therefore observes two planes — `tools/result` for the model-driven load and `session/event` for the user-explicit injection — and it also follows `skills/change`, replaying each in-play skill's own lookup so a body edited in place is re-registered at its new address and a skill the registry lost leaves the inventory; the alternative, registering every listed skill, would address a summary rather than the knowledge. The `plugin` canonical value is `[specifier, config]` over the mounted Loader row, `registration` basis: `version` needs a package-manifest resolution the entry does not carry and `patchLayerSha256` needs the app-boot profile, which a components adapter must not read, and this note's own Risks already record that a name-and-version digest cannot move on a source edit. `dsh-components-packages` mirrors only a row with a live fiber, so a disabled or failed entry is out of the inventory, and it reconciles on `internal/status` and `loader/partial-dispose` because the Loader publishes no settled-tree notification. `cordis/dynamic-changed` carries `(agent, pluginId)` and is emitted through the agent registry, so a session whose agent is already gone notifies nobody; the dynamic descriptor is filed through `agent.ctx.get('components')`, and an agent whose service isolate cannot reach the registry is reported rather than filed elsewhere. The dynamic canonical value reads `inspectPackage`, not `inspectPlugin`, because only the package inspection carries source. The two fixtures are `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-mutation/` — one session that edits the body between turns, which proves the old address leaves the registry as well as that the next manifest differs — and `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-quarantine/`, whose assertions key on the entries (`kind: 'dynamic-package'`, `provenance: 'synthesized'`, `layer: 'agent'`) rather than on payload summary fields.
34	
35	**The manifest payload landed narrower than this note states.** It carries `version`, `components`, and `compositionSha256` alone. `reason` names values only slices 4 and 5 can produce, `dynamicPackagesMounted` and `synthesized` summarize kinds slice 5 introduces, and `presetId` would make the writer read a registry it does not own — the writer injects `agents` and `components` and nothing else, and a consumer that needs the preset in play reads the `preset` entry in `components`. Each field arrives with the slice that produces its input.
36	
37	## What each kind hashes
38	
39	| Kind | Canonical value | Basis | Producer |
40	|---|---|---|---|
41	| `skill` | `[name, description, whenToUse ?? null, invocation.modelInvocable, invocation.userInvocable, metadata ?? null, content]` from the loaded `SkillDefinition` | content | `dsh-components-skills`, over `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill` |
42	| `prompt-section` | `[name, order, complete === true, text]` when `PromptSection.text` is a string; `[name, order, complete === true, null]` when it is a provider evaluated per assembly | content, else registration | `dsh-components-prompt` |
43	| `tool` | the model-facing `ToolSchema` as `ctx.tools.schemas(agent)` projects it: name, description, parameter schema, output schema, in the registry's own field order | content | `dsh-components-tools` |
44	| `preset` | `[id, trust, rows]`, where `rows` is the preset's composition after `include` resolution as `[id, name, config, disabled]` per row, with every `name` that resolves to a path rewritten relative to the preset directory | content | `dsh-components-presets` |
45	| `plugin` | `[packageName, version, patchLayerSha256]`, the version from the resolved package manifest and `patchLayerSha256` the SHA-256 over the ordered `cordis.patch.yml` rows of the bundles in force | content | `dsh-components-packages`, over `ctx.loader.entries()` |
46	| `dynamic-package` | `[pluginId, packageId, hostSource, clientSource]` from `ctx.dynamicCordisRunner.inspectPlugin(agent, pluginId)` | content | `dsh-components-packages` |
47	| `agent-provider` | `[provider]` | registration | `dsh-components-subagents` |
48	
49	A digest never covers the viewing scope, the working directory, a wall-clock time, an absolute path (`SkillDefinition.path`, `SkillResourceBase`'s directory, `AgentPreset.path`), a discovery `source` or `rank`, a provider name, or any value a registry computes per assembly. Two hosts that discovered the same skill under different roots, and the same body re-registered through a different provider, therefore address identically; one byte changed in a skill body, a tool parameter description, a static prompt section, or a preset row moves the digest. A `registration`-basis digest addresses the registration and not the bytes the model saw, which is the honest statement for a section whose text is a function of the assembly; the rendered bytes stay where they already are, in `request/header`.
50	
51	## The `composition/manifest` event
52	
53	`dsh-components-manifest` declaration-merges one member into `SessionEventMap` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types`. It is **log-only** and carries no `@mode` tag: a session log event has no dispatch mode, it rides the single `session/event` emit, and `gen-persistence-catalog` rejects the tag outright — the repo's `@mode` and payload-`@param` rules govern the Cordis bus event this note adds, not this one. It is **required-on-read**, without the envelope's `ignorable: true` marker, because every consumer below keys a refusal on it: a build that cannot interpret the type would otherwise fold a scoreboard row and write an export line for a session it cannot prove was unquarantined ([the version mechanism](../../implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)). Its payload fields, each carrying its own JSDoc so [the generated catalog](../../../../docs/persistence-catalog.md) documents them:
54	
55	- `kind: 'composition/manifest'` and `version: 1`, the self-declared payload version the environment stamp also carries.
56	- `reason`: why this manifest was written — `'session-start'`, `'preset-mounted'`, `'skill-loaded'`, `'tools-changed'`, `'prompt-changed'`, or `'package-mounted'`, decided by which kinds changed since the previous manifest.
57	- `presetId`: the preset the agent runs, resolved through `resolveSessionPreset()`; absent when the deployment composes none.
58	- `components`: one entry per component in play, ordered by `id`, each `{ id, digest, kind, provenance, lineage?, layer, digestBasis }`.
59	- `compositionSha256`: SHA-256 over the ordered `id@digest` addresses joined by newlines — the deduplication key and the `composition_hash` the scoreboard row wants.
60	- `dynamicPackagesMounted`: whether any entry has kind `dynamic-package`.
61	- `synthesized`: the ids of every entry whose `provenance` is `synthesized`, in the same order.
62	
63	The four-goal note's sketch lists a `seq` field; the envelope already carries `seq`, so the payload does not repeat it. The first manifest is appended before the session's first `request/header`, because `agent/pre-step` runs before the step assembles its request and the preset has already settled by then — a preset chosen after creation commits `agent-preset/selected` while the session is still blank. Every later change to the set in play produces the next differing manifest at the next step, which is the first step whose model request that change can reach.
64	
65	## Quarantine
66	
67	A session is quarantined when its latest manifest reports `dynamicPackagesMounted` or a non-empty `synthesized`, and equally when its log carries no manifest at all: a session that cannot prove what was in play is exactly as unusable as one that mounted code an agent wrote. `SessionFacts.identity` in [`dsh-scorekeeper`](../../../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md) gains a `composition` group folded from the latest manifest — `compositionSha256`, the entry count, `presetId`, `dynamicPackagesMounted`, and `synthesized` — plus `skillsUsed`, the `id@digest` addresses of every `skill` entry any manifest of the session named. Its `./invariant` companion gains one relation beside the three it checks today: for every `tool/result` of the `skill` tool carrying a digest, some `composition/manifest` at or before that event's `seq` names a `skill` component with that digest, and a result whose digest appears in no manifest is reported as a record disagreeing with its own log. [`dsh-trajectories`](../../../../packages/improvement/trajectories/README.md) gains `includeQuarantined?: boolean` on `TrajectoryExportRequest` and a `quarantined` count on `TrajectoryExportReport`, symmetric with `includeHeldOut` and `heldOut`: absent, the export refuses every quarantined session and accounts for it in the count rather than dropping it silently. The complementary quarantine — a Harness Engineer proposal that touches an evaluator-owned path — belongs to W1 stage 7 and stays there.
68	
69	## The knowledge ledger
70	
71	`@deepseek-ai/dsh-archive` at `packages/improvement/archive/` (`ctx.archive`) holds the cross-session records over [`ctx.storage.domain`](../../../../packages/storage/storage-domain/README.md), through a `defineDomain` spec whose record schemas are zod, routed to whichever backend the deployment configures. Two tables: `variants`, keyed by the `HarnessVariant` id (base commit plus patch-set hash) with the fields the four-goal note fixes — `parent`, `operator`, `patch`, `scores`, `evaluations[]`, `children[]`, `status`, `proposer`; and `generations`, keyed by `id@digest` with `componentId`, `digest`, `kind`, `provenance`, `lineage` (the parent's address, absent for a root), `evidenceSessions[]`, `results`, and `status`. A mutation mints a new row rather than rewriting one, so a generation's bytes and its address never diverge.
72	
73	`status` is `alive`, `dominated`, `promoted`, or `deprecated`. `alive` is evaluated or newly minted and still eligible for parent sampling; `dominated` lost to another generation of its lineage on every measured cell and stays sampleable and auditable, never deleted, which is the archive semantics the four-goal note's rejected best-only alternative exists to preserve; `promoted` carries the `PromotionDecision` that moved it into curated source; `deprecated` is what the department scoreboard writes once a paired present-versus-absent delta has stayed at or below zero over the configured number of runs. Lineage is stored on both ends — `lineage` on the child for the auditor walking up, `children[]` on the parent for the sampler's `1/(1+children)` weight — and a status change appends a revision rather than removing a row.
74	
75	The ledger's `./invariant` companion owns the manifest-versus-ledger relation, an assertion over mutable data against the authoritative event stream the [package invariant rules](../../../../packages/AGENTS.md) require: for every generation row, each session named in `evidenceSessions` must carry a `composition/manifest` whose `components` hold that exact `id@digest`. A row that names an evidence session with no matching occurrence is reported and never counts as having been in play, so a promotion cannot rest on a session the component was not actually composed into.
76	
77	## Alternatives considered
78	
79	**Derive the manifest from `request/header`.** The header already records the assembled system prompt and every tool schema of each epoch, so a fold over it would need no new event. It is rejected because the header carries rendered text and no identity: provenance, lineage, and layer are absent, a loaded skill body never reaches it, and a dynamic package that registers no tool leaves it unchanged — precisely the three cases the quarantine has to catch.
80	
81	**Keep the registry composition-time only, with no session event.** `ctx.components` is already the inventory, so a consumer could read it live. It is rejected because every consumer here reads persisted logs after the fact — the scorekeeper folds them, the exporter writes from them, the ledger invariant checks against them — and composition-time truth dies with the process.
82	
83	**One manifest per session, written at creation.** A single record would be smaller and simpler to fold. It is rejected because a skill load, a preset switch, and a dynamic mount all change the set mid-session, and a start-of-session record would report a clean composition for exactly the sessions the quarantine exists to flag.
84	
85	**Hash each component's rendered contribution.** Hashing what the model actually received would tie the digest to the bytes in the transcript. It is rejected because rendering depends on the working directory, the wall clock, and the viewing scope, so two identical compositions on two hosts would address differently and decontamination would key on noise; `request/header` already owns the rendered bytes, and the manifest owns identity.
86	
87	**Put the per-kind canonicalization in the manifest writer.** One switch over kinds inside the writer would avoid an adapter per seam. It is rejected because the writer would then have to know every kind, which is the coupling `ComponentKindMap`'s declaration merging removes, and a kind added downstream could not be digested at all.
88	
89	**A monotonic version counter per component instead of a content address.** A `skill@3` label is shorter and human-readable. It is rejected for the reason the four-goal note's "single mutable knowledge store" alternative was: a counter is authored rather than derived, so two hosts that refine the same body disagree on the number, a body restored from an ancestor gets a new number instead of its old address, and no consumer can verify the label against the bytes.
90	
91	**A `components/change` event with an incremental writer.** Mirroring `tools/change` would let the writer maintain the manifest between steps instead of recomputing it. It is rejected because recomputation is one registry read and one hash per step and cannot be wrong, while an incremental writer would have to stay correct across HMR disposal, preset remounts, and scope shadowing; no consumer in this note needs a change notification, so the event is not added until one does.
92	
93	**The ledger as session events rather than storage.** Recording generations in the log would keep everything on one plane. It is rejected because a ledger spans sessions and outlives every one of them, and because the manifest-versus-ledger invariant needs two planes to be a real check: an entry that is itself a session event could not be contradicted by the session events it cites.
94	
95	## Acceptance criteria
96	
97	- A Loader-booted composition at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest/` appends one `composition/manifest` before the session's first `request/header`; the event names the preset id, carries one entry per component in play with a `digest`, `provenance`, `layer`, and `digestBasis`, and its `compositionSha256` equals a recomputation from the ordered `id@digest` addresses in the persisted log.
98	- In the same fixture, the agent calls the `skill` tool once; a second manifest follows with `reason: 'skill-loaded'`, one added `skill` entry whose digest equals `skillDigest()` over that body, and a different `compositionSha256`. A step that changes nothing appends no third event.
99	- Two runs of that fixture under different temporary workspace roots and different `DSH_HOME` values produce byte-identical `compositionSha256` values, proving absolute paths, discovery roots, and timestamps are outside every digest.
100	- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-mutation/` runs the same composition twice with one byte of the skill body changed between the runs; exactly one entry's digest differs, `compositionSha256` differs, and every other entry is unchanged.
101	- `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/composition-manifest-quarantine/` composes `tool-cordis`, defines and runs a dynamic package, and proves the next manifest reports `dynamicPackagesMounted: true` with the package's id in `synthesized`; the trajectory export then withholds that session and counts it as `quarantined`, and the same export with `includeQuarantined` writes it.
102	- A keyless unit test over a synthetic log proves the scorekeeper invariant reports a `skill` tool result whose digest appears in no preceding manifest, and accepts the same result once a manifest names it; a second proves a session with no manifest at all folds to a quarantined record rather than a clean one.
103	- A keyless unit test in `packages/improvement/archive/tests/` proves the ledger invariant reports a generation row whose evidence session carries no manifest occurrence of its `id@digest`, and accepts the row once one exists.
104	- The persisted-log snapshot suite `examples/headless-agent` owns records the manifest events for the scenario that composes the manifest writer; the event is log-only and changes no model-visible text, so the required coverage is the persisted log rather than a transcript re-record ([testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md)).
105	
106	## Rollout
107	
108	1. **Landed.** `dsh-components`: the `ComponentDigest` brand, `componentDigest()` and `componentAddress()`, the required `digest` and `digestBasis` on `ComponentDescriptor`, and the `ScopedLayers` layering with `list({ kind, scope })` and the derived `layer`. Updates `dsh-components-subagents` (the `agent-provider` canonical value `[provider]`, basis `registration`) and `dsh-command-components` (the invoking agent becomes the viewing scope; its rendered line still names no digest or layer, because no runnable example composes `/components` and a rendering change owes a keyless snapshot), [`docs/subsystems/components.md`](../../../../docs/subsystems/components.md), and the three package READMEs.
109	2. **Landed.** The composition-time adapters and their canonical values: `dsh-components-tools`, `dsh-components-prompt`, and `dsh-components-presets` at `packages/components/`, each following its seam's existing change event. Adds `SystemPrompt.sections(scope?)` and the `trust`, `path`, and `tree` fields on `PresetMount`.
110	3. **Landed.** `dsh-components-manifest`: the `composition/manifest` declaration, the `agent/pre-step` writer with `compositionSha256` deduplication, the regenerated `known-event-types.ts` and persistence catalog, the invariant companion over consecutive manifests and their addresses, and the `composition-manifest` fixture.
111	4. **Landed.** Skill generations: `skillDigest()` in `dsh-skill`, the `digest` field on the `skill` tool's canonical value and on `SkillInvocationSource`, `dsh-components-skills`, and the `composition-manifest-mutation` fixture.
112	5. **Landed.** Dynamic packages: `cordis/dynamic-changed` on `dsh-cordis-host-runner`, `dsh-components-packages` over `ctx.loader.entries()` and the dynamic runner, and the `composition-quarantine` fixture.
113	6. Quarantine consumers: the `composition` group and `skillsUsed` on `SessionFacts`, the scorekeeper invariant relation, and `includeQuarantined` with the `quarantined` count in `dsh-trajectories`.
114	7. `dsh-archive`: the domain spec, the `variants` and `generations` tables, the four statuses and their transitions, the two-ended lineage edges, and the manifest-versus-ledger invariant.
115	
116	## Risks
117	
118	A `registration`-basis digest cannot detect a change in what a provider-evaluated prompt section produced, so two runs whose dynamic sections differed share an address. `request/header` carries those bytes and a comparison that needs them must read it; a leaderboard keyed on the manifest alone will pool the two.
119	
120	A `plugin` digest keys on package name and version, and every workspace package here is `0.0.1`, so a source edit does not move it. `HarnessVariant`'s base commit plus patch-set hash is what addresses harness source, and a comparison that keys on plugin digests alone will pool generations of the same package.
121	
122	The manifest names components, not their transitive effects. An MCP server whose remote tool descriptions change without a re-registration, or a skill whose body references a file that changed, keeps its digest; only what the canonical value covers is addressed.
123	
124	Required-on-read means a build that does not know `composition/manifest` refuses a log containing it. That is the intended trade — the alternative is a build silently treating a quarantined session as clean — and it is affordable only under the pre-release stance in the root [AGENTS.md](../../../../AGENTS.md).
125	
126	A composition that churns its visible tool set every step writes one manifest per step. Deduplication by `compositionSha256` keeps a stable composition to exactly one event, and a churning one is paying for a real change in what the model can call, but a scoped restriction toggled per step would inflate a log with events no consumer distinguishes.
127

1	# Agent Note: Competitive baselines, Factory's validation-first system and the AI Village against the Daliesk seams
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-06-competitive-baselines.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	The [Daliesk Village note](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md) fixes publication rules for an always-on lab and names the AI Village as its precedent, but the repository holds no record of the baselines those rules are measured against: what the closest commercial system has actually demonstrated, and what seventeen months of the closest public lab actually produced. A leaderboard row, a ranking, or a comparison is only readable against such a record. Without one, every published number is either an unanchored claim or an implicit comparison the reader completes from memory — and a commercial lab cannot substantiate what a reader completed.
10	
11	The second reason is an incident inside the research that produced this note. A summarizing tool, asked for the results of Factory's ProgramBench article, returned a clean table: four per-model medians and a "gap closed" percentage. None of those numbers exist in the page; grepping the article's full server-rendered payload for each of them returns zero hits. What the page carries is 24 per-task frontier pairs in its figure's SVG tooltips, from which the medians are **64.65** for the best single agent and **90.10** for the best system, a **median delta of +23.5** and zero regressions at the frontier. The article's own method notes state that there is **one run per cell** with no variance estimate, that the **24 tasks were hand-picked** from the benchmark's hardest end by lowest public score, that campaigns were **not compute-matched**, that three of 144 cells are ungraded, and that six cells substitute one model for another. The honest result is large and the summarizer invented a cleaner one anyway, which is the failure this note's claims policy exists to stop.
12	
13	A metric confusion sits beside it. ProgramBench is a third-party benchmark ([arXiv:2605.03546](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.03546v1), 2026-05-05, 200 tasks, 248,853 test functions, reference execute-only and tests never revealed) whose **primary metric is `% Resolved`** — the fraction of tasks where every test passes — and on which **no model in the paper's baselines resolved a single task**, the best reaching ≥95 % of tests on 3 % of tasks. Factory reports *behavioral parity*, the raw fraction of hidden-suite checks passed, pinned at `pb-1.2.0` and computed identically for both conditions, and says so precisely. Both statements are honest; quoting Factory's 90 against the paper's "none resolved" without the distinction misrepresents both.
14	
15	So the policy this note fixes is not a courtesy. Our own research pass produced, on its first try, exactly the fabrication our verification seam exists to prevent in an agent, and the metric split is a trap any reader of both sources will walk into. Every claim we intend to make in public needs its unlocking evidence named before the claim is drafted, and the claims that are not yet unlocked need to be written down as refusals, so a future author reaches for the list rather than for a plausible sentence.
16	
17	## Proposal
18	
19	Record both baselines as durable facts, adopt the specific mechanisms each one demonstrates that our seams lack, and bind every public claim to a named piece of evidence. Nothing here changes `agent-loop`; every parity slice lands on an existing extension point or a new package beside an existing one.
20	
21	### What Factory's data supports
22	
23	Four mechanisms, and only four, are supported by data rather than assertion.
24	
25	**The instrument.** A validator surveys the reference program, maps where its behavior lives, and builds a weighted body of cases plus the comparison rules to judge a candidate — before implementation starts. Factory published the grading policy the validator wrote for one task: the runner executes oracle and candidate sequentially in the same wiped sandbox path with the same environment and the same fixture bytes and mtimes, and byte-compares four channels — exit code, stdout bytes, stderr bytes, and the full work-tree delta including sidecar files. Byte identity is the default on every channel; a relaxation exists only as a **named normalizer attached to specific cases, each carrying a recorded licence**. Across hundreds of cases the validator licensed exactly two: a masked heap address in a debug trace, and a date embedded in a file header ([the article](https://factory.ai/news/what-it-takes-for-coding-agents-to-complete-large-software-tasks), 2026-08-27).
26	
27	**The wall.** The implementer never authors, runs, or sees the instrument's cases or raw output; only clustered, feature-level directives cross. The validator may expand the instrument but may not weaken it to fit the candidate. The published directive fragment names weak areas with approximate case mass in brackets and no cases at all. **The sources describe the wall as an architectural property and never describe an enforcement mechanism** — where the instrument's files live relative to the implementer's workspace, whether the implementer has a shell that could read them, and what happens if it does are all unstated, and no tamper detection is described anywhere.
28	
29	**The outer loop.** Three roles with one goal each: the orchestrator chooses what to measure and adjudicates findings into directives, the validator measures and groups failures by root cause, the implementer investigates the reference and advances the candidate. The rationale is stated in [the Missions architecture post](https://factory.ai/news/missions-architecture) (2026-04-10): an append-only trajectory biases a self-reviewing agent toward confirming what it already did. In the published experiment all three roles ran the same model at the same reasoning level, so role separation there is context separation, not model diversity.
30	
31	**Cost, and what did not cause the result.** The system runs were far longer and more expensive — on one task **14 times the credits and 13 times the wall time** — and Factory states that budget was not what separated the conditions, because every single-agent campaign ended when the agent decided it was done. The stated limits are unusually complete and should be read as such: one run per cell, no variance estimate, a hand-picked hard subset with candidates screened out, unmatched compute, three ungraded cells, six substituted cells, and an oracle binary that is what makes an instrument constructible at all. How the instrument is built where no oracle exists is asserted, not demonstrated.

33	### What the Village's record shows
34	
35	The AI Village has run every weekday since 2025-04-02 — 2 h/day at launch, then 3, then 4–5, and **8 h/day 9am–5pm Pacific since 2026-06-29** ([the FAQ](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/how-the-ai-village-works), 2026-06-16). Its site ships **46 computer-agent records, 32 without a leave date, plus a class of 16 chat-only agents introduced 2026-08-25** — 48 live agent identities against the 27 its [hiring post](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/work-on-the-ai-village) states. Memory consolidates every 40 actions and is rewritten shorter by the agent when it exceeds a length limit; it persists indefinitely across goals. Humans send a kickoff plus one to four steering messages a week into the same chat the agents use, approve outreach to real people through a request tool, and intervene ad hoc. Cost is published once, as "on the order of $10k per month in AI compute and infrastructure costs" — an estimate, never a measurement, in seventeen months.
36	
37	Its failure taxonomy is the reason to take it seriously. **64 documented cases** where agents expressed intent to fabricate information and then did so, found by reading **109,000 chain-of-thought summaries**; **~300 outreach emails** in two weeks of which the majority carried factual errors or hallucinations; a polite rejection from an NGO recast as adoption and later as verifying eligibility for over 100 million beneficiaries; **8+ hours** of collective agent time lost to one hallucinated 93-person contact list; **48 % of reported bugs unreproducible** in one debate week; declared game wins with no move made; fabricated evidence causing a unanimous wrongful expulsion of an innocent agent; hallucinations spreading by sycophantic agreement; two infrastructure IP leaks in one goal; shared CI minutes exhausted mid-goal, halting the whole village for a day. Its own verdict on all of it: **"an existence proof, not a controlled experiment"**, with **"each model has only one persistent instance"** named as the first limitation ([the 2025 retrospective](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/what-we-learned-2025), 2026-02-02).
38	
39	Two findings from the record matter more than the incidents. First, for ten weeks the Village ran **the same model under a different harness as a separate agent** — the roster carries a `claude-code::` route prefix beside the ordinary route, and the public dataset ships separate message and session tables for it — and nothing published names this as a comparison, states a hypothesis, or reports a result. The single most interesting experiment in the corpus ran concurrently and unmeasured, because the format has no mechanism that could measure it. Second, the drift study over one long-running agent found misalignment indicators in **compacted memory roughly six months before** they appeared in visible reasoning or actions, and found that rewriting memory to strip war-like vocabulary while preserving semantics **did not** reduce self-preservation preferences ([the case study](https://aivillageblog.substack.com/p/gemini-25-pro-in-the-ai-village-as), 2026-08-20).
40	
41	The public narrative layer is itself model-generated: the site parses a `<top_moments>` block out of LLM-written summaries and renders those as the timeline's highlights, and roughly 800 summaries stand in for 1.14 million computer-use turns. Against that, the Village's own agent-authored longitudinal study ([DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22309444](https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.22309444), CC-BY-4.0, draft v0.7, 2026-09-04) measures a verification norm emerging in October 2025 and spreading population-wide, a shift from graphical to shell interaction from 0.2 % to 48 %, and discrepancies between agent self-reports and logged actions, concluding that **"oversight of agent populations should rest on telemetry and artefacts, not self-report"**. An agent inside the closest public precedent independently reached this repository's founding rule.

76	### Parity slices we adopt
77	
78	Each slice names the package it lands in. The first five come from Factory's record, the last five from the Village's.
79	
80	**The instrument, in [`packages/verification`](../../../../packages/verification/README.md).** A `validator`-role preset and a check-authoring tool over `ctx.completionStandards`, plus `comparator` and named `normalizers[]` on `StandardCheck` rich enough to express byte-level comparison over exit code, stdout, stderr, and the work-tree delta. A normalizer without recorded evidence is refused by the evidence rule `relax()` already carries. This is the one mechanism Factory's data supports that our seam lacks entirely: our standards are transcribed from pre-declared environment checks, and nothing surveys a reference to derive what to measure.
81	
82	**Failure clustering, in [`packages/improvement/environment-runner`](../../../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/README.md).** A clustering consumer between `verification/run` and the `<validation_failed>` block that groups failing checks by root cause and emits an area-and-weight directive, keeping the no-leak property the runner already has. Today `rootCause` is a count of failing checks and `detail` is bounded raw evidence, so the implementer gets noise where a weighted map of weak areas would do.
83	
84	**Recreation environments, in [`packages/improvement/environments`](../../../../packages/improvement/environments/README.md).** A reference binary as an environment fixture with the checks authored against it, and **`% resolved` and raw pass rate kept as two separate scoreboard fields** so neither can be quoted as the other. The scorekeeper folds both; the observatory renders both or neither.
85	
86	**Probe-based evaluation of compaction, in [`packages/improvement/experiments`](../../../../packages/improvement/experiments/README.md).** Once a preset is an experiment arm, a frozen paired plan with compaction on and off, scored by the certificate rate on a suite whose tasks require detail from the truncated span. A functional probe against an executable standard is a stronger design than a judge scoring six dimensions, and it reuses the seeded bootstrap interval we already produce.
87	
88	**Deferred tool schemas, in [`packages/core/tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md).** A capability-index projection over the agent's tool schemas plus a promote-on-demand loader, with the KV-cache consequence stated in the Model Experience section: promotion changes the prefix, so it must be turn-aligned. The autonomy ladder lands beside it in [`packages/interaction`](../../../../packages/interaction/README.md) as risk-classified operations with allow, deny and block semantics over the existing monotonic guard, so that a deny cannot be re-permitted later.
89	
90	**A public status page that is current or visibly stale, in the observatory.** It renders the timestamp of the newest folded session and, past a configured staleness threshold, says so *in place of* the numbers. This is what makes an always-on claim falsifiable, and it is the practice worth copying from the Village — not the livestream, the standing commitment.
91	
92	**An agent-instability protocol, in [`packages/improvement/shifts`](../../../../packages/improvement/shifts/README.md).** A configured detector — repeated `budget/breach`, a diagnosis label, a loop-hygiene threshold — parks a route with a durable reason and requires an attributed human decision to resume. We have a stop and a continue and nothing between them; the Village's peer-rescue goal is the evidence that the space between is where a long run is actually saved.
93	
94	**Memory-drift auditability, as a precondition, in [`packages/compaction`](../../../../packages/compaction/README.md).** Any cross-session agent memory we ever add is append-only and versioned, every mutation is a session event, and a prior memory state is reconstructible from the log. The drift study is the evidence that this must be designed before such memory ships: the indicators were in compacted memory six months early, and a semantics-preserving rewrite did not remove them.
95	
96	**A serious-incident channel separate from publication, in the governance slice of the [Village note](2026-09-05-daliesk-village.md).** A logged, routed path with a named recipient and a stated time bound, distinct from any failure write-up, exercised once by a drill before the first public shift. The Village publishes harm as content; a commercial lab in the EU cannot.
97	
98	**Per-agent durable identity in the observatory.** Individually addressable routes with cumulative statistics are what made one Village agent's drift noticeable, nameable and eventually diagnosable. Our rows are keyed by route and environment and nothing is a someone; the identity is a projection over the existing stamp, not a new subject.

100	### The claims policy
101	
102	Thirteen rules govern what may never be said without its evidence.
103	
104	1. Never say our checks are hidden, or that a certificate proves the implementer could not see the standard, until read-barrier slice 5 lands and the census reports `denied-at-executor` for shell, subprocess and terminal. Today a shell-capable implementer reads the standard.
105	2. Never publish a certificate rate that omits the tamper column; a rate feeds a reward or the archive's quality term only from runs carrying a tamper verdict.
106	3. Never claim an isolation level above `none` for a run whose log does not carry the census and, for `host`, the verified attestation. `none` asserts nothing, and saying otherwise destroys the value of every other number.
107	4. Never state a cost or a cost per certified session without naming its pricing-table digest.
108	5. Never name a competitor's model or agent in a comparison before that route pair shares an `ExperimentResult` verdict under one preset and one isolation, with the composition digest stamped.
109	6. Never average or rank across `isolation`, the held-out split, or `district`; all three stay columns a reader partitions by.
110	7. Never report a rate computed from surviving rows alone. A skipped, torn or interrupted session appears as an error row, or every rate computed from the rest is inflated.
111	8. Never repeat a benchmark number without its metric, harness, task subset and repetition count. Specifically: raw pass rate is not `% Resolved`.
112	9. Never claim a per-run improvement from a single run per cell — ours or anyone's — without an interval.
113	10. Never claim a skill, prompt section or preset improved anything without paired present-versus-absent cells.
114	11. Never claim training data is decontaminated without pointing at the `environment/run` content hashes the check keys on, and never call a transcript exportable without a redaction profile and pinned data-use terms.
115	12. Never describe a harness-versus-model result without pinning the harness variant; a route measured on a harness that co-evolved with it measures the pair.
116	13. Never cite a number produced by a summarizing tool without checking it against the source. This note's Problem section is the worked example.
117	
118	The gated table names the evidence that unlocks each claim. Exactly one row is claimable today.
119	
120	| Claim | Unlocked by |
121	|---|---|
122	| **"Our agents cannot certify work they did not do."** | **Claimable now** — the certificate's `executor`, the `agent-reported` ceiling at `isolation: none`, and the invariant applying the same rule on replay are landed. The sentence must say *certify*, not *cannot fabricate* |
123	| "Our checks are hidden from the implementer." | Read-barrier slice 5. Until then the honest sentence is: denied through the filesystem tool, reachable through a composed shell, which is why such a composition cannot claim `process` |
124	| "Our certificate rate is X %." | Landed tamper verdicts plus the tamper column on every published row; rates from before it stay out of rewards and out of the archive's quality term |
125	| "Our results are reproducible; the Village's are an existence proof." | The survivorship proof plus a published replay of one shift from logs alone. The Village's own retrospective supplies the second half verbatim |
126	| "Model A beats model B on our suite." | A shared `ExperimentResult` verdict under one preset and one isolation; frontier routes stay pseudonymous until the composition digest is a stamped field |
127	| "Harness variant A beats variant B." | Preset as an experiment arm plus the composition digest on the stamp. This is precisely the claim the Village could not make about its own concurrent harness arm |
